correctness.rationale: Puncturing is an isomorphism between two \(k\)-dimensional codes. The source characterization forces projection rank \(\ell\), hence kernel dimension \(k-\ell\). For an \(r\)-subcode \(U\), \(t=\dim Q(U)\) satisfies the stated rank range; old support is bounded by both \(d_r(C)\) and \(d_{r-t}(K)\), while new support is at least \(t\). This proves the lower bound. Lifting a source minimizer proves the upper bound, and full projection gives terminal equality. Exhaustive small-code replay independently checks all finite ingredients.

value.rationale: The source introduces shortest LCD embeddings to improve code quality while adding the minimum number of coordinates. Generalized Hamming weights are the canonical higher-dimensional support refinement of minimum distance. The theorem shows that hull dimension imposes unavoidable support growth across the upper hierarchy and identifies a kernel invariant that can sharpen it. The self-orthogonal specialization gives the reusable all-r law \(d_r(\widetilde C)\ge d_r(C)+r\).
